record.paper_title: Advances and Open Problems in Federated Learning
record.original_question: Can the multi-task or lifelong-learning perspective used for personalization and privacy in federated learning be extended to other phenomena such as concept drift, and can non-parameter-transfer lifelong-learning methods such as ProtoNets be made useful in federated learning?

evidence.quote: Several challenging FL topics including personalization and privacy have begun to be studied in this multi-task/LTL framework [270, 250, 299]. Is it possible for other issues such as concept drift to also be analyzed in this way, for example as a problem in lifelong learning [420]? • Can non-parameter transfer LTL algorithms, such as ProtoNets [425], be of use for FL?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the federated learning setting in which a central coordinator collaborates with a population of clients i = 1, ..., N, each holding a local data distribution D_i, to learn personalized predictive models f_i without centralizing raw data. A multi-task / learning-to-learn (LTL) viewpoint regards each client's task as drawn from a meta-distribution over tasks, and seeks shared representations or meta-parameters that transfer across clients. Concept drift refers to the phenomenon in which a client's data distribution D_i(t) changes over time t, so that the optimal predictor f_i(t) is non-stationary. Lifelong learning algorithms aim to continually learn a sequence of tasks while retaining performance on earlier ones; among them, parameter-transfer methods (e.g., MAML-style approaches) share weights across tasks, while non-parameter-transfer methods such as Prototypical Networks (ProtoNets) operate by computing class prototypes in an embedding space and classifying new points by nearest-prototype rules, without transferring task-specific parameters.

Address the following two questions:

(a) Formulate concept drift in federated learning as a lifelong-learning problem within the multi-task / LTL framework. Specifically, design an algorithmic framework and provide a theoretical analysis (e.g., generalization or regret bounds) for federated learning under client-side concept drift, treating the temporal sequence of distributions {D_i(t)} on each client as a stream of related tasks to be learned in a lifelong-learning sense.

(b) Design and analyze a federated learning algorithm based on a non-parameter-transfer lifelong-learning method such as Prototypical Networks. Determine whether such non-parameter-transfer schemes can be made useful in federated learning, and characterize conditions under which they yield provable benefits (in accuracy, communication cost, privacy, or robustness to heterogeneity) over parameter-transfer-based federated meta-learning approaches.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as a forward-looking research direction in the federated learning literature. Subsequent work has explored federated continual/lifelong learning and federated prototype-based methods (e.g., FedProto and federated continual learning frameworks), but no definitive resolution of the broad questions—unifying concept drift with the multi-task/LTL framework and establishing the general usefulness of non-parameter-transfer LTL algorithms like ProtoNets in FL—has been established. The questions remain open as broad research programs.

status_evidence.title: FedProto: Federated Prototype Learning across Heterogeneous Clients
status_evidence.snippet: We propose FedProto, where clients and server communicate abstract class prototypes instead of model parameters, addressing heterogeneity in federated learning.
status_evidence.claim: Non-parameter-transfer prototype-based methods have been adapted to federated learning, providing partial progress on question (b), but the general program remains open.

status_evidence.title: Federated Continual Learning with Weighted Inter-client Transfer
status_evidence.snippet: We introduce a federated continual learning framework that addresses catastrophic forgetting and inter-client interference in non-stationary federated environments.
status_evidence.claim: Federated continual/lifelong learning frameworks have been proposed to handle non-stationarity, indicating partial progress on question (a) but no comprehensive theoretical resolution.
